current_bottleneck.diagnosis: The public path is bulk rather than coefficient-at-a-time. It nevertheless rebuilds normalized part lists in ordinary Python, converts already-exact ZZ entries to BigInt, and then unnecessarily round-trips its byte stream through one enormous exact integer.

lowering.ingress: Encode canonical SJPZ/SJPQ bytes once, create one generated owned FlintByteRegion with one host-to-foreign copy, borrow it synchronously while parsing, and close it in finally.
lowering.host_fast_path: For an exact list, feed ZZ values directly to exact_integer_values_to_packed_bytes and canonical QQ values directly to canonical_rational_values_to_packed_bytes. Fall back to the ordinary coercion loop only when the checked primitive declines the input.
lowering.ownership: The returned polynomial is independent of the temporary byte region; validation failure publishes no resource and leaks neither owner.
lowering.node: Use the generated byte-region from-bytes adapter; no handwritten operation-specific N-API and no stream-sized BigInt transport.
lowering.wasm: Copy the canonical stream into linear/owned foreign memory, borrow it for the same parser, and preserve the packed dynamic fallback when FLINT resources are unavailable.

invariants: ordinary CPython-parseable public Python remains the source of construction semantics
trailing zero coefficients are removed and all zero inputs produce the unique zero polynomial
QQ coefficients are normalized with positive coprime denominators before publication
arbitrarily skewed coefficient sizes require no uniform per-entry limb capacity
one public construction performs no coefficient-at-a-time foreign calls
already-canonical host lists do not allocate a second Python list of scalar parts
one public construction performs at most one host-to-foreign byte-stream copy on Node
FLINT-to-FLINT polynomial operations never serialize through this ingress format
the canonical SJPZ/SJPQ wire format and SagePack round trips remain unchanged
invalid or unrepresentable streams fail transactionally with deterministic cleanup
semantic_differentials: one highly skewed 65538-bit coefficient among small coefficients
canonical rational signs, zeros, and large relatively-prime denominators
degree, selected coefficient access, equality, and SagePack round trip
invalid coefficient coercion leaves no partially published resource
generated-resource capability disabled uses the correct packed fallback

acceptance.correctness: All semantic differentials agree between generated-resource execution, capability-disabled packed execution, and SageMath where formats are comparable.
acceptance.boundary: Generated adapter audit proves one checked host-list packing pass, one byte-region ingress, one borrowed parse, zero scalar coefficient calls, and no stream-sized BigInt.
acceptance.performance: On each measured host, report fresh-process setup, first invocation, and a warm median separately. For 5001 small dense coefficients, warm public construction for both ZZ[x] and QQ[x] must be no slower than 2.0x SageMath on the same host. Also test 20001 coefficients and skewed inputs for linear scaling in coefficient count plus encoded bytes; never encode a single-host crossover as a universal constant.
acceptance.portability: Linux x64 and macOS arm64 must exercise the generated resource; Windows x64 and Wasm require either that path or a tested correct capability fallback.
acceptance.maintainability: The implementation adds declarations and ordinary Python wiring but no compiler branch specific to polynomial construction.

stage_gates.canonical_pack: The benchmark must time the checked direct host-list pack separately for ZZ and QQ, and a route/audit test must prove that public canonical-list construction actually uses it rather than merely leaving the primitive available.
stage_gates.byte_region: The benchmark must time region creation and the borrowed FLINT parse separately; audit must reject Buffer reverse/hex, stream-sized BigInt, and fmpz payload marshalling in the public constructor.
stage_gates.end_to_end: The same benchmark must retain public first and warm measurements. Passing only the ByteRegion stage or only the canonical-pack stage is insufficient: both route assertions and the end-to-end same-host SageMath ratio must pass.
stage_gates.skew: Run the public path with one 65538-bit value among small values and report encoded bytes; time and memory must scale with total encoded bytes, not maximum limb size times coefficient count.
